steps.description: With the fluorocarbon on your left hand, make a loop and hold it in place.
With the braided line on your right hand, thread the braided line into the loop you just made with the fluorocarbon.
Loop your braided line around the fluorocarbon 6-12 times and thread it back onto the fluorocarbon's loop.
Cinch the knot by carefully pulling on the two ends of your line.
With the hook on your left hand and your line on your right, carefully thread the line onto the eye of the hook or lure.
After threading the line onto the eye, make a loop and carefully wrap the line onto the hook and your existing line for at least 6-12 wraps.
While holding in place the wraps you have made, carefully thread the line end onto the loop you have made.
After threading the line end onto the loop, carefully pull on the line from your right hand to tighten it.
With the hook on your left hand and your line on your right, carefully thread the line onto the eye of the hook or lure.
After threading the line onto the eye, leave a small loop and carefully wrap your line for at least 6-12 wraps.
After wrapping your line, thread back the line end onto the small loop you have left out, and back to secure it.
Carefully tighten using your right hand to lock it in place.
First step is to secure your line onto your reel by making a simple knot.
Secure the line you have made and put the cover back to the reel.
After assembling the reel, you may slowly reel in your line to fill up your reel's line holder.
Once filled, you may cut the excess line and store it for later use.
To assemble the rod, prepare your reel and rod on a flat surface.
To attach the reel onto the rod, gently align the bottom of the reel onto the rod's reel slot and tighten the knobs to secure it in place.
Next up is to thread your line onto the ring guides. Ensure that each ring guide has been passed.
This finishes your rod setup and now you're ready to tie in your hook or lures!
